c.tagline: Portuguese colonial charm beneath dazzling lights.

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the crowded Senado Square–Ruins of St Paul's stretch, and casino areas attract loan-shark and money-changing scams.

hood_desc: The historic core of the city blending Portuguese colonial architecture, temples, and old casinos with dense local life, ideal for heritage sightseeing and travelers wanting authentic Macanese character.
A charming district with a preserved old village of narrow lanes, colonial houses, and renowned Macanese and Portuguese eateries, great for foodies and those seeking old-world atmosphere.
The glitzy reclaimed strip of mega-resorts, casinos, and lavish shows modeled on Las Vegas, suiting luxury seekers, gamblers, and families visiting themed resorts.
A quiet, green, laid-back island retreat with beaches, hiking trails, and the famous Lord Stow's egg tarts, perfect for those wanting to escape the casino crowds and relax.
The iconic paved central square with its wave-patterned tiles, colonial buildings, and shops, a bustling sightseeing and shopping hub at the heart of the historic center.

water.note: Tap water meets WHO standards and is safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buses charge a flat MOP 6 (~US$0.75) — pay exact cash on board or use a Macau Pass card from convenience stores. The LRT sells single-trip tickets from station machines and also takes Macau Pass. Mobile QR payments (MPay, Alipay) work on most buses.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am to midnight with a few overnight N routes; the LRT runs about 6:30am to 11:15pm.
transit.note: Free casino and hotel shuttle buses link the ferry terminals, border crossings, airport and Cotai resorts — many visitors get around mainly on these.
